Context. The previous page sets up a Gaussian-integer analogue of Gauss's lemma for the biquadratic (quartic) residue character [p/P]. Take a system of 'least residues' α mod P. For ξ+iη = αp/P, the class of α is read off from the parities of [2ξ] and [2η]: class 0 = (0,0), 1 = (1,0), 2 = (1,1), 3 = (0,1). This page is a numerical test case with p = 1+2i and P = 7+12i. The next page tabulates the class counts k0, k', k'', k''' for p = 1+2i and many P.

(1) Data. P = 7+12i has N(P) = 49+144 = 193, a prime ≡ 1 (mod 4); p = 1+2i has N(p) = 5. Gauss notes 4·48+1 = 193, so (193−1)/4 = 48. This is the number of residues in a quarter-system: one per associate class of the 192 nonzero residues.

(2) Main formula. 2(x+iy)(1+2i)/(7+12i) = (2/193)(x+iy)(1+2i)(7−12i). Here (1+2i)(7−12i) = 31+2i. Hence the expression equals (2/193)[(31x−2y) + (2x+31y)i]. This gives 2ξ, 2η for α = x+iy as linear forms in x, y.

(3) Boundary tests. These are, on my reading, checks whether particular α lie inside the region 0 < ξ', η' < 1/2, where α/P = ξ'+iη'.
- 2(2+3i)(1+2i)/P = (112+194i)/193. Note (2+3i)(1+2i) = −4+7i. The line '2(−4+7i)/(7+12i) = 112/193 + 194/193 i' is the same number computed directly. So 2α/P for α = −4+7i has imaginary part 194/193 > 1, i.e. −4+7i lies just outside the region.
- 2(3+5i)/P = (2·81 − 2i)/193, since (3+5i)(7−12i) = 81−i. The imaginary part is slightly negative, so 3+5i is just outside.
- '1+3i: 50/193 + 190/193 i' is 2(1+3i)(1+2i)/P = 2(−5+5i)/P. The left-margin scratch '−35, +60, −95+25i, 50' is this multiplication: (−5+5i)(7−12i) = −35+60+(60+35)i = 25+95i, and i·(25+95i) = −95+25i; doubling gives 50+190i. The number −5+5i also appears in the list at the lower left.

(4) Cell diagram. The small figure shows the 3×3 unit-grid (= half-unit in ξ, η) partition of the square spanned by p and ip, with counts
1 7 2
7 9 8
2 8 4
- The counts total 48. The row sums 10, 24, 14 are written beside the figure.
- With the class pattern from the previous page (0 1 0 / 3 2 3 / 0 1 0) the class counts are: class 0: 1+2+2+4 = 9; class 1: 7+8 = 15; class 2: 9; class 3: 7+8 = 15.
- [My inference] The Gauss-lemma analogue predicts [p/P] = i^(Σ class) = i^(15+18+45) = i^78 = i^2 = −1.
- The large figure at the top is an enlarged drawing of the same configuration: a 3×3 grid with the inscribed tilted square of side vector (2,1) ~ 1+2i, inside a slightly rotated larger square (the image of the residue square).

(5) Corner location. 't+it = 3½+6i' with '2t+4u = 7, 2t−u = 6' gives u = 1/5, t = 31/10 (Gauss writes 31/10). This means 7+12i = t(2+4i) + u(4−2i) = 2(1+2i)(t−iu). So P/2 = (1+2i)(31−2i)/10 locates the corner P/2 in coordinates adapted to p.

(6) Check by direct power. '[(1+2i)/(7+12i)]^48 ≡ α+bi (mod 193)' is the definition of the quartic character via Euler's criterion. 'α − 7b/12' reduces α+bi to a rational integer mod 193, because 7+12i ≡ 0 gives i ≡ −7/12.
- [Mine, completing] 12^{-1} ≡ −16, so i ≡ 112 (mod 193); indeed 112^2 ≡ −1.
- Then 1+2i ≡ 225 ≡ 32 = 2^5, and 32^48 = 2^240 ≡ 2^48 ≡ −1. This holds because 193 is not of the form x^2+64y^2, so 2 is a quadratic but not a quartic residue.
- So [(1+2i)/(7+12i)] = −1 = i^2, agreeing with the lattice count in (4).

(7) The 4×4 table with heads 1, i, −1, −i (only the first entry, 1, filled) is an unfinished table of unit/class combinations. The list 7+12i, 7−12i, −5+5i, −3−2i, 1−i and the notes 'p i, q i, −2, +2' are unclear scratch (possibly a reduction chain). I do not reconstruct them.

The line '2 3+5i/(7+12i) = 2·81/193 − 2/193 i' omits the factor (1+2i) used in the neighbouring lines. It is correct as 2(3+5i)/P, a test of α itself rather than of αp. Likewise '2(−4+7i)/P' equals 2(2+3i)(1+2i)/P, so the two lines are consistent rather than contradictory.
The individual cell counts 1,7,2/7,9,8/2,8,4 cannot be verified from the image alone. Their total (48) and the resulting character (−1) are consistent with the direct computation.

results.what: Numerical determination of the quartic residue character [(1+2i)/(7+12i)] = −1 by counting the classes (parities of [2ξ], [2η]) of αp/P over a quarter residue system of 48 elements, i.e. a Gaussian-integer analogue of Gauss's lemma / lattice-point count.
results.modern_name: Gauss's lemma for the biquadratic (quartic) residue symbol in Z[i]; lattice-point proof approach to biquadratic reciprocity
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Nachlass, published in Werke II); Eisenstein (1844) for published Gauss-lemma-type proofs of biquadratic reciprocity

results.what: Quartic character via Euler's criterion: (1+2i)^48 mod 7+12i, reduced to an integer congruence mod 193 using i ≡ −7/12 ≡ 112.
results.modern_name: Euler criterion for the quartic residue symbol; reduction of Z[i]/(π) to F_p

results.what: Linear form 2αp/P = (2/193)[(31x−2y)+(2x+31y)i] and boundary checks of lattice points, plus solving for P/2 in p-adapted coordinates (t = 31/10, u = 1/5).
results.modern_name: Explicit coordinates of the lattice map α ↦ αp/P

deep.surprise_reason: This is a worked numerical example of Gauss's known (Nachlass) Gauss-lemma approach to biquadratic residues. It contains concrete counts (1,7,2/7,9,8/2,8,4) confirming [(1+2i)/(7+12i)] = −1. That is a nice unpublished detail but no new result; the method itself is known as Gauss's from Werke II.
